The positive binomial series and Tonelli give s^r Beta(1-r,2r) 2F1(r,1-r;1+r;s)=r Beta(1-r,2r) B_s(r,r). Reflection and B_s(r,r)+B_(1-s)(r,r)=Beta(r,r) give the total r Beta(1-r,2r) Beta(r,r)=Gamma(r)Gamma(1-r). At s=0 the integral is Beta(r,1-r) directly; s=1 follows by reflection. As an independent classical check, rescaling the known potential on [-1,1] gives pi/cos(pi a/2)=Gamma(r)Gamma(1-r). The mass Beta(1-r,1-r)/[Gamma(r)Gamma(1-r)] simplifies to the printed M_a. f_a is in L2 iff 2r<1 iff a>0. For phi in B, ||psi(t)||_B=f_a(t)||phi||_B, so psi is in X_pos despite the unbounded time weight. Then q_sigma=phi for every sigma, h_sigma=Gamma*phi is time-constant, v_psi=M_a int phi Gamma*phi, and I_psi is the whole-H1 Rayleigh rate of that potential. No d>=2 theorem, rough flow, Gaussian point value or mass renormalization is needed.

checks.claim: C6: diagnostics, preserved failure, corrected quadrature and no overclaim
checks.reason: By inspection, attempt01 and the successor differ only in lines 13 and 15, so identity, 50 digits, 1e-18 tolerance and case list are unchanged. The substitution is correct by hand: t=s(1-u^p) and s+(1-s)u^p with p=1/(1-a) and Jacobian s^(1-a)/(1-a). The successor is an exact algebraic factorization of t(1-t) with expm1, with no clipping, regularizer or loosened assertion, so it resolves the rounding without masking a defect. Failure at a=0.1, s=1 is plausible because t=1-u^p can round to 1 as u approaches 0, while s=0 does not form that subtraction. JSON values agree with my hand evaluation to the digits I computed.
